author: massicomar
title: Boredom
summary:
Alex doesn't like boredom. That's why whenever he gets bored, he comes up with games. One long winter evening he came up with a game and decided to play it.

Given a sequence a consisting of n integers. The player can make several steps. In a single step he can choose an element of the sequence (let's denote it ak) and delete it, at that all elements equal to ak + 1 and ak - 1 also must be deleted from the sequence. That step brings ak points to the player.

Alex is a perfectionist, so he decided to get as many points as possible. Help him.

Input

The first line contains integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 105) that shows how many numbers are in Alex's sequence.

The second line contains n integers a1, a2, ..., an (1 ≤ ai ≤ 105).

Output

Print a single integer — the maximum number of points that Alex can earn.
explanation: Order in the array doesn't matter: group equal values. Taking value v earns v·cnt[v] and forbids v ± 1 — house robber over values.

extraLayers.prompt: What should the DP state represent?

options.text: dp[x] = max points using only values ≤ x
dp[i] = max points using the first i array elements
options.why: Deleting a_k ± 1 removes elements anywhere in the array; index order is meaningless.

options.text: dp[l][r] = max points from subarray l..r

extraLayers.explanation: Re-index by value: the conflict is between v and v ± 1, i.e. neighbours on the value line.

extraLayers.prompt: Given that state, which transition is right?

options.why: Takes both x and x−1, which conflict.
Taking x takes every copy of x: multiply by its count.

options.text: Always take the largest remaining value
options.why: Greedy fails: for {1, 2, 2, 2, 3}, taking 3 first deletes the 2s (total 4), while taking the 2s gives 6.

extraLayers.explanation: Either skip value x, or take all copies of x and jump back over x−1.

es.explanation: El orden en el arreglo no importa: agrupa los valores iguales. Tomar el valor v suma v·cnt[v] y prohíbe v ± 1: es house robber sobre los valores.
traps: La respuesta puede pasarse de 32 bits (1e5 · 1e5).

dp-state.explanation: Reindexa por valor: el conflicto es entre v y v ± 1, o sea, vecinos en la recta de valores.

why.b: Borrar a_k ± 1 elimina elementos en cualquier parte del arreglo; el orden de los índices no significa nada.
why.c: Acá no hay estructura de intervalos.

dp-transition.explanation: O bien omites el valor x, o tomas todas las copias de x y saltas por encima de x−1.

why.b: Toma x y x−1 a la vez, y esos están en conflicto.
why.c: Tomar x es tomar todas las copias de x: multiplica por su cantidad.
why.d: Greedy falla: con {1, 2, 2, 2, 3}, tomar primero el 3 borra los 2 (total 4), mientras que tomar los 2 da 6.
